subject: Post-call: Medix eval scope, dataset template & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery follow-up: proposed eval plan & dataset needs

Hi Sara — thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap and a suggested path forward so we all have the same checklist.

Call recap (30m):
- Medix goal: improve triage accuracy for intake forms and standardize patient routing (clinical/non-clinical).
- Primary UX: short free-text -> normalized routing labels + short justification string.
- Success criteria you mentioned: 95% routing accuracy on core 7 intents, <5% hallucination/unsupported routing.

Proposed Redwood-run eval (what we offer):
1) Run a set of 3 candidate models across your dataset and compare: accuracy, per-label recall, hallucination rate, avg latency, token cost.
2) Provide per-example diff CSV and top error clusters + suggested prompt/temperature adjustments.
3) Deliver a short technical report and a prioritized prompt set for canary.

What we need from you to start:
- A ~2k-sample JSONL dataset (see attached medix_promptset_v1.jsonl) with fields: id, input, reference_label, reference_justification.
- Scoring rubric: how do you weight accuracy vs hallucination vs coverage? (we suggested a default below)
- Any PII constraints or preferred upload method (S3 presigned, secure Drive share, or run on Redwood Private).

Suggested default scoring (we can adjust):
- Primary metric: exact-match accuracy on reference_label (0.7 weight)
- Secondary: hallucination rate (0.2 weight) — responses that include false clinical assertions or invent procedures
- Latency/cost: measured but not part of the quality score (0.1 informational)

Next steps / timeline:
- You share sample dataset + rubric by 2026-01-19.
- Rishi will set up the eval harness on a sandbox Dedicated instance and run baseline within 3 business days of receipt.
- We'll schedule a 30m results review the week after the run.

Attachments: medix_promptset_v1.jsonl (sample schema), redwood_eval_checklist_v2.pdf

If this looks good I’ll open the HubSpot milestone and ticket Rishi can use for infra.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0112

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@medixhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-10T13:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: proposed eval plan & dataset needs

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our end: 

1) Data/privacy: We prefer the eval to run in our VPC (Redwood Private) because the intake content can include PHI. Is that supported for this sandbox run? If not, we can anonymize but would prefer not to.
2) Scoring: your suggested weighting makes sense. For hallucination detection, do you have an automated classifier or is it manual review? We expect you to capture false clinical assertions automatically where possible.
3) Dataset template: the attached looks fine — one ask: please include a field `sensitivity_flag` (low/medium/high) so we can exclude high-sensitivity examples if needed.

We can deliver the 2k sample by 2026-01-18 if we lean on our data team. We will provide either a secured S3 presigned link or a Private deploy token.

Can you confirm whether you’ll include model configuration (temperature, top_p, max_tokens) in the report? Also curious which model variants you typically recommend for routing tasks (smaller faster models vs larger instruction-tuned ones).

Thanks —
Sara Patel
Director, Data Science — Medix Health
sara.patel@medixhealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@medixhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-11T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: proposed eval plan & dataset needs

Hi Sara — quick technical note on how we recommend you format the dataset and how we’ll score it on our end. We can run in your VPC if you want Redwood Private — that’s straightforward and preferred for PHI.

Dataset format (JSONL, one JSON per line):
- id: string (unique)
- input: string (raw intake text)
- reference_label: string (one of the canonical 7 intents)
- reference_justification: string (short free-text explaining the label)
- sensitivity_flag: string (low|medium|high)  -- we will exclude high if you request
- metadata: string (comma-separated or JSON-encoded as a string)

Sizing guidance:
- 2k total is great: aim for 70% train-like / 30% edge / OOD. We’ll subsample to create a representative test shard (n=2000 -> eval on 2k as requested).

Automated scoring approach (outline):
1) Normalized label match -> exact / fuzzy match (primary accuracy).
2) Hallucination detection: rule-based heuristics + a small ML classifier we maintain that flags clinical assertions not supported by the input; we will flag and sample for human review.
3) Coverage & confidence: measure token-level coverage and model confidence distribution; bucket by input length (<=50, 50-150, >150 tokens).

Threshold suggestions (initial):
- Exact-match accuracy >= 0.95 for core intents
- Hallucination rate <= 5%
- Median latency (p95) < 120ms on Dedicated baseline

Output artifacts we will provide:
- Per-example predictions CSV with model outputs and scores (sample attached: sample_eval_results.csv)
- Summary dashboard: per-model metrics + error clusters + prioritized prompt changes
- Diff CSV for quick import into your bug tracker

If you want, I can drop a small script (python) to validate your JSONL and produce a presigned S3 upload target. Otherwise, share an S3 presigned link and we’ll pull it into the Private sandbox.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-12T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: proposed eval plan & dataset needs

Sara — thanks, and great — Private sandbox works. Confirming next steps and owners: 

- Medix (Sara): share 2k JSONL sample + indication of whether `sensitivity_flag=high` should be excluded by 2026-01-18. Preferred upload: S3 presigned link to `redwood-medix-eval` bucket.
- Redwood (Rishi): once we have the link, we’ll validate format (same day), spin up a Private sandbox and run the baseline on 3 candidate models (Rishi to pick candidate variants: one small/fast, one mid-size instruction-tuned, one high-accuracy).
- Redwood (Karthik): I’ll create the HubSpot milestone and calendar invite for the results review (target week of 2026-01-25).

Deliverables: baseline report, per-example CSV, dashboard link, recommended prompts & config (temp/top_p/max_tokens) to reach the target thresholds.

I’ve attached the checklist and a sample prompt set (medix_promptset_v1.jsonl). My team will also include the exact model names we test in the final report.

If that timeline works I’ll mark the HubSpot stage as "eval_in_progress".

Best —
Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
